headline: Bidisha Siddique arrested from Gulshan restaurant
summary: The former wife of ex-president Hussain Muhammad Ershad was apprehended by police on Tuesday night.
details: Bidisha Siddique, the former wife of former President Hussain Muhammad Ershad, was arrested on Tuesday night at approximately 8:30 PM.
Gulshan Police arrested her from the Arabica restaurant in Gulshan, Dhaka.
The arrest follows a fraud case filed in February 2008 during the tenure of the caretaker government at the Gulshan Police Station.
Bidisha Siddique had been sentenced to two years in prison in connection with this case.
The Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Gulshan Police Station confirmed that an arrest warrant had been issued against her.
caption:
Arrested from a restaurant in Gulshan: Bidisha Siddique, former wife of ex-president Hussain Muhammad Ershad, is back in custody.

Bidisha Siddique, the former wife of former President Hussain Muhammad Ershad, was arrested on Tuesday night at approximately 8:30 PM.

Gulshan Police arrested her from the Arabica restaurant in Gulshan, Dhaka.

The arrest follows a fraud case filed in February 2008 during the tenure of the caretaker government at the Gulshan Police Station.

Bidisha Siddique had been sentenced to two years in prison in connection with this case.

The Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Gulshan Police Station confirmed that an arrest warrant had been issued against her.

headline: Govt not inclined to spend public money on Brazil friendly match in Bangladesh
summary: State Minister for Youth and Sports Aminul Haque says hosting the world champions is not a priority amid struggles with electricity and fuel expenses.
details: State Minister for Youth and Sports Aminul Haque stated that bringing the Brazil national football team to Bangladesh is not a priority while the country struggles with electricity and other essential sectors.
Haque noted that the government is not inclined to spend public funds on a single match given the high expenses currently faced in power and energy sectors.

The statement comes after a five-member delegation from the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) visited the National Stadium and Bashundhara Kings Arena to assess the possibility of a friendly match.

While acknowledging that the match would be a major achievement and a dream for fans, Haque expressed skepticism about whether it would actually transform the long-term development of Bangladesh football.
The Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) views the CBF visit as a positive development and may seek government assistance if the proposal moves forward.
Haque indicated that government support would depend largely on the BFF's ability to secure private sponsorships to fund the event.
The State Minister clarified that discussions regarding the match are still in the very preliminary stages and no open discussions on expenses have taken place yet.
caption:
Would a match against Brazil transform Bangladesh football? The government says no—and it's not a priority right now.

State Minister for Youth and Sports Aminul Haque stated that bringing the Brazil national football team to Bangladesh is not a priority while the country struggles with electricity and other essential sectors.

Haque noted that the government is not inclined to spend public funds on a single match given the high expenses currently faced in power and energy sectors.

The statement comes after a five-member delegation from the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) visited the National Stadium and Bashundhara Kings Arena to assess the possibility of a friendly match.

While acknowledging that the match would be a major achievement and a dream for fans, Haque expressed skepticism about whether it would actually transform the long-term development of Bangladesh football.

The Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) views the CBF visit as a positive development and may seek government assistance if the proposal moves forward.

Haque indicated that government support would depend largely on the BFF's ability to secure private sponsorships to fund the event.

The State Minister clarified that discussions regarding the match are still in the very preliminary stages and no open discussions on expenses have taken place yet.
